documents.title: Orpheus (topherchris420/orpheus-resonance-protocol)
documents.text:
Browser-based tactical simulation with generated mission events, squad state, visual pacing controls, and an optional microphone-reactive audio layer. The interface is an interactive fiction and systems-design prototype.

What is real: When explicitly enabled for the current visit, the browser reads microphone audio energy locally and uses it to vary a visual glow and generated tones. What is generated: Threats, intel, pulse, respiration, HRV, stress, cohesion, and recommendations. Audio energy cannot establish those physiological values. This app is not a medical, biometric, or operational decision system.

documents.title: Orpheus — A command room where every choice leaves a trace
documents.text:
Orpheus puts you inside a changing fictional situation. Read the map, weigh competing courses of action, and see how your choices change modeled pressure, cohesion, and objective progress. Then open the after-action review: each committed choice has a phase, a timestamp, and an explicit set of consequences.

Try a complete session:

1. Choose Enter simulation. The theatrical terminal is optional; no account, API key, or microphone is required.
2. Open Decisions. Inspect the tradeoffs and commit one course for an event. Its alternatives close for this visit, even if you switch views.
3. Use Advance phase to reveal later events and unlock the red-team controls. Phases stay under your control by default; Auto advance optionally advances every 30 seconds.
4. Switch back to Situation map whenever you want. Opening decisions no longer replaces the map permanently.
5. Open After-action to review your decisions and objective progress. Download session JSON preserves the record before you refresh.

What makes the loop work:

- One authoritative decision ledger. The model accepts only available event/outcome pairs, resolves effects from its own catalog, and rejects repeated or conflicting commitments. Pending events replenish the shortlist.
- Inspectable consequences. Choices apply deterministic, bounded changes to simulated pressure, stress, cohesion, and objectives. Displayed authored weights are metadata, not calibrated success probabilities; no probability draw is performed.
- Reviewable sessions. Exports include the decision ledger, objective snapshot, up to 120 recent events, and 48 chart samples with source labels. No raw microphone data or activation phrase is included.
- Optional sensory layer. Explicit per-visit microphone consent enables local audio-energy response. Generated tones start at zero gain, have a fixed output cap, and stop with the microphone control.
- Desktop and mobile surfaces. A persistent session bar provides map, decisions, phase controls, and review. Mobile tabs keep the dense panels navigable.

Boundaries of the model:

The tactical world and telemetry use random generators; a full session is not deterministically replayable. Only the catalog decision transition is deterministic for a given state and choice. The review remains live while the world advances. Objective percentages are authored scenario bookkeeping, not validated measures of success or operator performance. Refresh starts a fresh decision session; preferences may persist locally. Exports are snapshots, not authenticated audit logs.

- The activation screen provides no access control. For a protected deployment, enforce identity, authorization, and audit logging on a server.

documents.title: ascent. (topherchris420/project-ascent)
documents.text:
Your home is more than a number. Understand the evidence behind it.

A home estimate should begin a conversation, not end one.

Ascent is a free, open-source real estate intelligence tool built for homeowners. Explore recorded sales, understand how a price was calculated, test the financial consequences of a decision, and take the reasoning with you.

No professional license. No subscription. No account required for the public pricing studios.

Look up your home: one address box searches every covered market.

Explore DC homes · Explore Maryland homes · Explore DC condos · Try a fictional example

My Home · Published accuracy · Free-service promise · Live application

documents.title: ascent. — The question isn't just "What is my home worth?"
documents.text:
It's why, compared with what, and what happens if I choose differently?

Imagine you are considering selling. Someone gives you a number. Usually, that's where the explanation stops.

Ascent lets you investigate the number instead:

1. See the sales. Inspect the recorded comparable properties, their differences, their adjustments, and how much each one influences the estimate.
2. Challenge the assumptions. Test a different condition rating, exclude a questionable comparable with a reason, or explore another asking price.
3. Explore the decision. Examine illustrative selling proceeds and, with your own financial inputs, compare selling, holding, renting, renovating before sale, refinancing, or buying while keeping your current home.
4. Keep the evidence. Save a versioned Property Evidence Passport on your device, revisit changed assumptions, and export a report you can examine, print, or share.

You see recorded facts, calculated estimates, your assumptions, and unknowns as different things. Ascent does not present an adjusted-sale range as a statistical confidence interval or a scenario as a forecast.

metadata.section: The question isn't just "What is my home worth?"

documents.title: ascent. — Find your starting point
documents.text:
The homepage and My Home share one address search. Try a DC house, Maryland home, or DC condo with the example buttons, use the arrow keys to browse matches, and press Escape or Clear address to start again. If one market is unavailable, successful results stay usable and a retry is offered. The mobile menu keeps saved homes, accuracy results, and help within reach.

Your question — Where to go — Coverage and caution
What supports the price of a DC house? — DC Pricing Studio — Eligible District single-family and rowhouse sales in a bounded public-record snapshot
What about my Maryland home? — Maryland Pricing Studio — Montgomery and Prince George's counties; bedroom/bathroom details are not available in this source
How do DC condo prices compare? — DC Condo Studio — Unit-level condo sales; the published condo accuracy study did not meet overall acceptance
Can I try this without a real address? — Interactive sample — Clearly fictional Arlington property; real pricing engine, illustrative evidence and assumptions
Where are my saved decisions? — My Home — Saved in this browser on this device; no account synchronization
What if I manage clients or offers? — Workspace entry — Fictional workspace demo or an empty private workspace when account services are configured

Start with the public studios. They work without a provider key, paid plan, or sign-in.

documents.title: ascent. — Built for decisions, not just estimates
documents.text:
01 · Make the price explain itself:

Inspect closed sales, distance, size, age, weighting, adjustments, exclusions, and source provenance. Explore sensitivity to individual inputs and compare asking-price scenarios. A changed assumption produces a changed calculation, not a hidden AI opinion.

02 · Follow the money:

The homeowner workbench connects property evidence to six deterministic ownership choices:

- Sell now
- Continue owning
- Rent the property
- Renovate before selling
- Refinance
- Buy another home while retaining this one

Enter your own debt, rates, expenses, rents, and other assumptions. The workbench calculates applicable payment schedules, monthly cash flow, equity, cash requirements, and break-even comparisons. Missing inputs stay unknown; Ascent does not quietly manufacture your mortgage, tax bill, rent, or renovation costs.

These are illustrative, pre-tax comparisons, not financial advice or predictions. They exclude important household considerations including replacement housing, tax effects, loan qualification, and financing availability. The choices do not represent equivalent housing outcomes and are not ranked as the best option for you.

How the homeowner workbench calculates and abstains

03 · Remember what changed:

A Property Evidence Passport brings the property's public evidence, your saved decisions, assumptions, and calculation versions into one reproducible history. Compare saved versions, see whether records or assumptions actually changed, and export a privacy-filtered JSON or standalone printable HTML report. Use your browser's Print command to save a PDF.

The Decision Time Machine distinguishes changed comparable evidence from changed homeowner assumptions. Its on-demand checks do not mean Ascent monitors the live market, fetches listings in the background, or sends price alerts.

04 · Ask for the explanation:

Ask Ascent can explain the calculations and evidence in context. Core pricing and homeowner financial computations are deterministic; AI does not set the home's price. Optional Groq/OpenAI integrations are separately configured, and production external-model synthesis remains blocked pending independent review.

metadata.section: Built for decisions, not just estimates

documents.title: ascent. — Our accuracy is public. So are the misses.
documents.text:
An impressive-looking price is not proof of accuracy. Ascent publishes reproducible retrospective tests, including criteria the models failed.

Market and model — Held-out sales — Median absolute percentage error — Estimates within ±10% of recorded sale price — Criteria met
DC single-family / rowhouses — 2,254 — 9.98% — 50.2% — 9/9, several narrowly
Maryland, revised model — 2,812 — 9.52% — 52.0% — 8/9; price-related bias criterion failed
DC condominiums — 1,434 — 12.95% — 41.16% — 4/9; overall acceptance failed

Published internal holdout studies as of October 18, 2026. Median error describes a tested group, not the expected error of your individual home. These are not independently certified results, appraisals, or guarantees.

A few distinctions matter:

- DC houses: Results depend on the exact validated configuration. Only that unmodified eligible configuration may display a calibrated interval; custom changes or insufficient evidence remove that claim. Several acceptance bars were met narrowly.
- Maryland: The revised study used a different holdout from an earlier failed model. Its improved headline number is not a like-for-like before/after comparison. One of nine criteria still fails; no current-home calibrated interval is released.
- DC condos: Five of nine acceptance criteria failed. Important building attributes such as HOA fees, floor, view, parking, and amenities are unmodeled. No calibrated interval is released.
- All markets: Public records may be delayed or incomplete. An adjusted comparable-price envelope is not automatically a calibrated probability interval.

Read the full results · Methodology, protocols and historical findings · Latest release and validation gates

documents.title: ascent. — What Ascent does not pretend to know
documents.text:
Ascent is not a live MLS feed, licensed appraisal, brokerage, or automatic transaction agent.

- Public address research currently covers qualifying Washington, DC houses and condos and Montgomery / Prince George's County, Maryland homes. It does not provide nationwide coverage.
- Virginia public-record pricing is not available. Written source-use permission remains unresolved. Neither an open-source license nor public website access creates MLS or provider redistribution rights.
- Listing status, concessions, property condition, renovations, title details, building characteristics, and other decisive facts can be missing.
- Seller scenarios do not predict buyer response, time on market, future prices, or renovation return on investment.
- Ascent does not autonomously message clients, make offers, sign contracts, or decide what someone should do.

Ascent is designed to make the limits visible alongside the evidence, not hide them in small print.

DC source scope · Maryland source scope · Condo model and limitations · Homeowner-first roadmap

- Removing a saved home asks you to confirm the address and history being deleted. …

documents.title: Quantum Noise Profiler (topherchris420/quantum-noise-profiler)
documents.text:
Every warning needs evidence.

**An open research instrument for tracking qubit noise, inspecting uncertainty,
and knowing when the data cannot support an answer.**

Quantum Noise Profiler (qnp) separates vendor calibration records, estimates
from ordinary workloads, and dedicated measurements. Its monitoring engine
reports the evidence behind each warning. Its offline explorer lets you inspect
the first physical-QPU experiment, down to the recorded shot counts.

Explore the evidence · Use the Python API · Results and limits · Reproduce

v0.3 research prototype · hardware warning accuracy is not established.
The simulation study passed 40/40 preregistered criteria. The first real-device
pilot challenged the constant-rate assumption in 6/10 readout series.
Both findings are part of the result.

documents.title: Quantum Noise Profiler — Explore the real hardware data
documents.text:
No IBM account, API key, quantum SDK or web server is needed. From a local clone:

git clone https://github.com/topherchris420/quantum-noise-profiler.git
cd quantum-noise-profiler
python -m pip install -e .
python -m qnp report

Open qnp-evidence.html in your browser. The report is self-contained and
works offline. You can also download the generated HTML snapshot
and open it locally; GitHub's file viewer does not execute HTML.

The explorer lets you:

- Inspect a qubit: compare both readout directions, step through 12 recorded
 batches, and see the underlying errors and shots. A shared vertical scale
 makes comparisons between qubits honest.
- Interpret a warning: locate recorded alerts without treating them as
 verified hardware failures. Historical vendor values are optional references.
- See where the model abstained: inspect every T1 fit, conditional interval,
 withheld estimate and reason code.
- Audit the evidence: review the original assumption checks, expand every
 simulation criterion, and export the plotted traces as CSV or the evidence
 bundle as JSON.

Before rendering, the exporter checks the displayed run entries and raw files
against MANIFEST.sha256, then reproduces probe rates and homogeneity statistics
from raw counts. It refuses missing or mismatched evidence and excludes fake,
rehearsal and smoke runs from hardware results. T1, alert and simulation summaries
are shown as recorded; the separate verifier recomputes those too.

python -m qnp report --results-dir results --output my-report.html
python -m qnp demo # deterministic synthetic example; prints strict JSON
qnp --help # equivalent installed command

Reports never overwrite results/. Use --force to replace an existing HTML
export. Explorer guide and verification scope →

documents.title: Quantum Noise Profiler — What the evidence says
documents.text:
A physical device challenged the model:

IBM ibm_fez · October 13–14, 2026 UTC · 5 qubits · 14 jobs · 296,000 shots.
Experiment P was a preregistered two-hour assumption check, not a test of whether
alerts predict real hardware failures.

Registered check — Recorded result — Interpretation
P.C1: a constant binomial error rate across 12 probe batches — 6/10 series reject; criterion failed — The constant-rate model did not describe these series adequately
P.C2: interleaved references detect readout drift within T1 sweeps — 0/10 sweeps reject; criterion passed — No within-job drift detected by this check; stability is not proved
T1 model checks — 7 estimates reported; 3 withheld — A number is withheld when coverage or fit diagnostics cannot support it
Recorded drift alerts — Five, on qubit 108 — Their true/false status is unknown without independent reference data

On qubit 108, p(0|1) rose from about 1% to nearly 3%, then partially recovered.
The explorer makes that excursion visible without assigning it an unverified
physical cause. Batch independence, generality across devices, and operational
value on hardware remain untested.

Hardware addendum · Complete v0.3 results · Proposed independent follow-up

Two simulation studies, including their failures:

Study — Result — What it establishes
v0.3 follow-up — 40/40 preregistered criteria passed — Improvements under the specified simulated conditions
v0.2 study — 53/62 preregistered checks passed — Useful improvements and explicit remaining failure modes
Physical pilot — P.C1 failed; P.C2 passed — Evidence about assumptions on one device over two hours

Selected v0.3 simulation results:

Question — v0.2 design — v0.3 design
Runs with a false alert after adding a 2 µs idle to an unchanged device — 1.00 — 0.02
Runs with a false alert after adding two-qubit gates — 0.43 — 0.05
T1 reported confidently wrong under slow readout drift (D11 conditions) — 0.255 — 0.005
T1 reported confidently wrong under linear readout drift of ±1.5% — 0.370 — 0.000

The false-alert rows use the empirically calibrated configuration, with 100
simulated runs per scenario. T1 rows use 200 fits per scenario and design.
These are observed simulation outcomes, not hardware guarantees.

In the closed-loop simulation, warnings plus daily calibration reduced jobs
run above 5% readout error from 13–20% to at most 0.31%. This uses illustrative
degradation rates and assumes recalibration on demand. Warnings did not
consistently reduce calibration overhead, and a calibrated CUSUM baseline
performed comparably. Cloud-user interventions such as remapping qubits have
not been validated.

Earlier results and unresolved limitations:

The v0.2 anytime-valid configuration raised an alert in at most 1% of stable
sessions across five simulated conditions. That is an observed rate, **not a
universal 1% guarantee**. The declared session budget is alpha_session = 0.10,
and each channel has its own null assumptions.

The 253-minute median warning lead came from a separate calibrated
configuration with empirical error control. At matched false-alert rates, it
outperformed a Shewhart baseline (223 minutes) and CUSUM (213 minutes) in that
scenario. Forecast coverage was measured across correlated forecasts within
runs, not independent hardware trials.

Failures remain instructive:

- A 10% step was detected within five batches in only 0.09 of runs, below the
 original 0.80 target. CUSUM remained better at detecting the smallest steps
 within 24 batches (0.64 versus 0.52).
- Stationary 10% fluctuations triggered alerts in about half of runs in an
 exploratory condition. The hardware pilot reinforces the need to model
 excess variation before deployment.
- Simulations omit leakage, coherent errors, crosstalk, 1/f dephasing and
 correlated multi-qubit errors. …

documents.title: rain-pipeline (topherchris420/rain-pipeline)
documents.text:
A hypothesis can fail. Its evidence should remain standing.

This is the reproducibility instrument behind a simple challenge: could someone inspect not only a scientific result, but the rules that were in force before the result appeared?

Inspect the failed experiment → · Read a passed run → · Set up and replay → · Verify the evidence chain → · Current R.A.I.N. Lab →

Three things to inspect first:

Question — Where the answer lives — Boundary
What was decided before the data? — Registered experiment specs and their Git history — A registration can be verified; it cannot prove no out-of-band data access occurred
What did the held-out records show? — The recorded results, including a failed test — A run can test its registered hypothesis, not every interpretation of its graphs
Could another machine regenerate the numerical result? — Replay receipts and verification contracts — Matching computations do not constitute independent replication with new subjects

The pipeline uses a pinned historical R.A.I.N. version from the former james_library as a submodule. The current integrated R.A.I.N. Lab lives in Lop Nur Twin; these experiments remain tied to the versions that originally produced them.

A mathematical question worth testing:

Can a preregistered effect survive a subject-level holdout and a falsifying negative control? The proposed study names assumptions, an existing baseline and a negative control. Candidate mathematics can be explored through R.A.I.N.'s shared reference scout. No additional mathematical capability has been demonstrated here yet.

documents.title: rain-pipeline — A note
documents.text:
I built rain-pipeline because I kept running into the same problem from different directions: a scientific result can look rigorous long before anyone has a reliable way to separate what was noticed, what was measured, and what was actually allowed to count as evidence.

I do not want another system that asks the reader to trust the researcher, the model, the paper, or even the software. I want the machinery of the claim to be visible.

That is the idea behind this repository. I am building a research system in which an observation can remain an observation, a hypothesis can be registered before it is tested, evidence can be tied to the exact bytes and code that produced it, failures can stay in the record, and another person can replay the result without needing to believe me first.

This is also how I think about my broader work at Vers3Dynamics. The point is not to manufacture certainty. The point is to build instruments that make uncertainty, provenance, and evidence harder to hide.

I am particularly interested in the boundary between human judgment and machine judgment. R.A.I.N. is not here to become an oracle. It is here to make the rules explicit, apply them consistently, and leave a trail that someone else can inspect.

So this README is intentionally a little more personal than a normal software README. The code is the artifact. The repository is the laboratory notebook. And the standard I am trying to hold myself to is simple:

Do not ask people to trust the result when you can give them the means to check it.

Everything that follows is an attempt to make that sentence executable.

documents.title: rain-pipeline — I. The problem is not dishonesty
documents.text:
The conscious and intelligent separation of what a researcher has noticed from what a researcher has shown is an important element in modern science. Those who maintain that separation constitute an invisible discipline. That discipline, not the eminence of the researcher and not the confidence of the prose, is the true source of a result's authority.

We're persuaded, our confidence won and our doubts settled, largely by mechanisms we have never examined. This is the natural consequence of the way the modern laboratory is organised. One mind looks at the data, forms a wish, writes the criteria, takes the measurement and announces the verdict; and the public, having no means of telling these five acts apart, hears them in one voice.

rain-pipeline is an instrument for giving them separate voices. It takes a question to a verdict on real data, and it keeps four things from being mistaken for one another:

where it lives — may it decide a verdict?
something we noticed — explorations/: analyses of data already seen, labelled exploratory — never
something we registered — experiments//experiment.json: write-once criteria, anchored by a git commit before the data is read — it defines what would
something we measured — runs/ and the R.A.I.N. run record: the registered measurements, each bound by hash to the bytes it came from — no; it is the input
something the registered criteria support — the verdict R.A.I.N. computes from those measurements and those criteria alone — yes, and nothing else does

metadata.section: I. The problem is not dishonesty

documents.title: rain-pipeline — II. Three sentences the public can carry
documents.text:
The group mind does not carry arguments. It carries phrases, and a principle the public can repeat is worth more than a proof it cannot. The instrument rests on three.

- Inference is not evidence. Explorations, the literature panel and every output a study computes but did not register stay description. None of them is ever submitted or evaluated.
- Evidence is not permission. A result cannot change its own criteria, reuse a holdout it has read, or speak for subjects it never saw. Registrations are write-once and git-anchored; a holdout is read once.
- Confidence is not authority. A verdict is as strong as the chain beneath it, no stronger. verify re-derives every link and grades every claim; replay re-executes it.

metadata.section: II. Three sentences the public can carry

documents.title: rain-pipeline — III. On the wish, which is older than the observation
documents.text:
A relation of mine in Vienna spent his life demonstrating that the wish precedes the perception, and that the mind which holds the wish is the last to be told of it. Researchers who look at the data and then write the criteria are not frauds. They are human beings, and the ordinary laws of the human mind apply to them with full force.

Every earlier remedy asked researchers to be better than that. This instrument asks nothing of the kind. It assumes the wish, and it arranges matters so that the wish does not matter. The criteria are written down, sealed by hash, committed to a public history and pushed before the pipeline first reads the designated holdout data; its ledger timestamps that first read. This makes the recorded process auditable. It cannot detect earlier or outside-the-tool access, and the author can still modify a public repository. The point is to expose the sequence, not declare the researcher's judgment infallible.

metadata.section: III. On the wish, which is older than the observation

documents.title: rain-pipeline — IV. Four separate roles, no borrowed authority
documents.text:
The strongest experiment is not the one with the most impressive referee. It is the one in which you can name who did which step, and check that no step quietly performed another's job.

The pipeline separates four roles. They are not four independent certifiers: the researcher maintains this software, writes the criteria and chooses what to investigate. The separation is implemented by contracts and recorded provenance, not by an external review board.

- R.A.I.N., the rules engine. The pinned historical version evaluates submitted measurements against registered criteria. A run cannot declare its own verdict; the author's software still defines how the criteria are evaluated.
- Anna, the librarian. Its cited literature record is sealed and re-verified by hash. Literature can inform a question but cannot overwrite criteria after registration.
- PhysioNet, the external data source. The Fantasia byte ranges read through the pipeline are logged with hashes, first-access times and reader identity. Replay refuses changed bytes. The ledger cannot detect data read outside this pipeline.
- Git history, the public timeline. A registration in a pushed commit is independently inspectable. It establishes the visible order of recorded commits and results, not a guarantee about everything the researcher did privately.

The aim is to make mistakes and interventions easier to detect and explain, not to claim external certification or perfect prevention of hindsight bias.

Each stage calls the upstream code in-process at a pinned commit (Anna, R.A.I.N. and DRR are submodules under vendor/). Nothing is copied or forked. Every run records which code ran, and verify maps that record back to the exact commit.

metadata.section: IV. Four separate roles, no borrowed authority

documents.title: rain-pipeline — V. The overt act
documents.text:
Opinion is not moved by argument. It is moved by an event the public can witness. When a nation was to be reminded what it owed the electric lamp, the counsel did not publish an essay; he arranged for the lamps of a continent to be dimmed and relit at an appointed hour, with the inventor present.

The event this instrument stages is smaller, and it is public. On 4 October 2026, at 17:41:53 UTC, commit 4b4a030 placed the criteria for V3D-EXP-0002 and V3D-EXP-0003 in the history of this repository, and that commit was pushed before the first byte of their held-out data was read. The commit, the push and the ledger are all open to inspection, and a reader who inspects them concludes without taking anyone's word for it.

documents.title: Project Sentinel — The experience
documents.text:
- An intentional starting point: Ground, Focus, Unwind, Rest, Clarity, and Explore preserve the original tone combinations with clear, descriptive names.
- A complete practice: choose 5–20 minutes, begin, pause, resume, or finish early. Sessions end automatically at the chosen duration.

documents.title: Resonate AI Mesh (topherchris420/resonate-ai-mesh)
documents.text:
The agent may propose a future. It does not get to authorize it.

Run the instrument → · Examine a blocked decision → · Replay the evidence → · Inspect the rules → · Read the limits →

Resonate AI Mesh is an executable research instrument for multi-agent decisions. Agents observe a simulated world and propose actions. The Pordenone kernel decides what may happen: deterministic validation first, then optional bounded judgment, then a versioned policy, and only then a commit. Every step is recorded in a hash-chained event log, so any run can be verified, replayed exactly without network access, explained decision by decision, and branched into counterfactuals. Experiments run those runs at scale with paired statistics.

Nothing here controls physical hardware. Human-state data is simulated unless a registered live source is connected, and no live source ships with the repository.

The cockpit above is replaying the canonical run. Judgment routed prop-00023-runner_02 to a person, and the simulated operator approved it. Re-validation then rejected it, because its observation had grown older than the 1500 ms limit while it waited. Human approval does not override a deterministic check either.

documents.title: Resonate AI Mesh — One decision under a microscope
documents.text:
The interesting artifact is not an agent's plan. It is the point where that plan fails to become an action.

The agent wants — The system requires — The evidence retains
To act on an observation — A deterministic check against the current state — What the agent observed, when, and whether it was still fresh
To ask a model for judgment — A proposal that already passed non-negotiable checks — The judge's bounded response, not a mutation of state
To proceed after human review — Re-validation before commit — An approval that can still be rejected
To explain why it acted — A policy-authorized state transition — Hash-linked events that can be replayed without calling the judge again

Try it: run make demo, find the human-approved but stale proposal in the narration, and compare the recorded decision with the cockpit screenshot. Then read the execution law, not just the outcome.

This tests the authority boundary under simulated hazards and operator actions. It does not demonstrate that a deployed assistant would be reliable on a customer's workflows.

Mathematical research question (experimental):

Do authorization invariants survive stale observations and competing agent proposals? This is a proposed experiment, not a new verified capability. Read the assumptions, negative control and protocol or use R.A.I.N.'s shared mathematics scout to inspect candidate openai/math references at its pinned revision. No OpenAI mathematics code or proof has been installed in this runtime.

documents.title: Resonate AI Mesh — One command
documents.text:
make demo # or: cargo run --release -p mesh-lab --bin mesh -- demo

No API keys and no network. In about a second this:

1. Records the Perturbed Mesh scenario: five agents, a hazard that appears mid-run, an operator-load spike, a sensor dropout, and a corrupted observation.
2. Narrates it from the recorded events, covering a deterministic rejection, a judged commit, a human review, and an injected fault.
3. Walks the causal chain of one decision.
4. Replays the run and verifies all 1424 events.
5. Re-runs it with judgment disabled and reports where the timelines diverge.

The cockpit runs with make cockpit, which serves mesh serve and Next.js together. A static export of real recorded runs needs no backend (pnpm --filter c2-dashboard dev).

documents.title: Resonate AI Mesh — The execution law
documents.text:
OBSERVE → PROPOSE → DETERMINISTIC VALIDATION → OPTIONAL BOUNDED JUDGMENT → POLICY → COMMIT / WITHHOLD → OBSERVE RESULT → RECORD + REPLAY

These hold by construction and are checked on every recorded run (see docs/architecture.md):

- No commit without a passing validation. AuthoritativeState::apply needs a CommitAuthorization. Only policy.rs can create one, and only from a ValidatedProposal, which only the validator can create.
- Judgment cannot override a failed check. Judgment is never consulted after a failed validation, and a human approval is re-validated before it commits.
- No remote model can mutate state. A judge returns an envelope and has no handle to state, the bus, the filesystem, or actuators.
- Replay makes no external calls. Networked judges and external agents are replaced by their recordings, and replay reports network_calls: 0.
- Data is labeled. Every event carries SIMULATED, LIVE, or REPLAY. Unlabeled data defaults to SIMULATED.

documents.title: Resonate AI Mesh — A reproducible experiment
documents.text:
mesh experiment run experiments/judgment-ablation/manifest.yaml

The manifest states a question, a hypothesis, and a pre-registered prediction. The run executes every condition at the same seeds (common random numbers) and writes summary.json, runs.csv, and report.md. The report gives means, medians, variances, t and bootstrap 95% intervals on paired differences, effect sizes, and a verdict on the prediction. Current results (SIMULATED, deterministic mock judges, not a language model):

Experiment — Finding (95% CI on the paired difference)
judgment-ablation — An evidence-based judge removes commits made on degraded evidence: −2.79 per run [−2.94, −2.64], 100 pairs, 0 unsafe commits in every condition. Replaying its recorded judgments reproduces the effect exactly. It does not change task success: difference 0.
validator-stress — Removing only the hazard-clearance check lets 9.12 unsafe proposals per run commit [8.90, 9.34]. The check is causal.
fault-injection — Under ten injected faults, every authority invariant held in all 440 runs. A lost human-state signal now fails closed (−3.9 commits). The earlier hold-last behavior silently disabled gating (+12.1).
human-state-adaptation — Operator-load gating withholds 31.9 background commits per run [−32.49, −31.35].
multi-agent-coordination — A minimum separation of 4 instead of 2 lowers task success by 0.21 [−0.28, −0.15].
resonance-routing — Consulting judgment only for unstable agents cuts judgment calls by 182 per run, but loses its protection (+2.55 degraded commits). The claim that it keeps protection is recorded as contradicted.

Ten claims in claims/ are checked against this evidence with mesh claims check. The checker never upgrades a claim: a person sets the status, and the tool reports whether the evidence agrees. See docs/experiments.md and docs/research-methodology.md.

Pine Gap

Humans and AI agents. One world. One set of rules.

 A browser-native 3D environment where a person and an AI agent attempt the same physical task

 through the same world mechanics, while their actions, outcomes and handovers are recorded for comparison.

The agent chooses what to try. The simulation decides what happens.

A pretty victory is not enough. Here, the controls, physics, failures and trace must tell the same story.

 ▶ Play as a human

In your browser.
Nothing to install.

 ▶ Watch an agent

No key needed. Press After Hours.

 ▶ Run Jev

complete live Jev run.

Jev at the controls, live. Free Roam's Borrowed Wheels (seed 48291), recorded in the browser through Let Jev Play on 3 October 2026: success in 143.7 s, 126 decisions, no failures or holds, 183 ms mean decision latency, 1,060 m driven, one pedestrian collision. Jev never touches the world: each decision becomes the same GameActions a keyboard and mouse produce, and the simulation decides what happens. The clip is re-rendered frame by frame from the run's trace with today's graphics, which replays the run exactly without calling Jev again, at 8× speed (MP4 · trace). The After Hours runs are below; the scripted baseline driving the After Hours coffee leg, filmed the same way on 5 October 2026 (delivered 100% in 87.5 s, at 10× speed), is here (MP4).

documents.title: satellite-vision-scape — Same world. Same controls. Same physics. Every action on record.
documents.text:
It is easy to make an agent look capable: give it an API that teleports it, a peek at the answer, a scorer that takes its word. Satellite Vision Scape does the opposite. A person and an agent enter the same simulation, their controls reach it through the same input path, and the world, not the agent, says what happened.

The setting is playable, cinematic and a little strange: a night shift at a reconstructed Pine Gap, a coffee run, a numbers station, four signal terminals and a midnight concert. That is deliberate. It makes a long, physical, multi-stage task that a person enjoys and an agent can fail at in instructive ways. But the thing being built is the instrument underneath: a shared world in which the behaviour of humans and AI agents can be recorded, measured, replayed and compared.

Note: What exists today: one Pine Gap environment, two documented task modes (After Hours and Free Roam), and human, scripted, seeded-random, replay and model-controlled runs. A complete live Jev After Hours session and a separate live Jev Borrowed Wheels session are recorded, not a repeated-trial success rate. This is not an environment-authoring tool, a multiplayer server, a sandbox for untrusted code or a server-attested benchmark. Details under Known limitations.

documents.title: satellite-vision-scape — How the experiment works
documents.text:
Every run, human or agent, follows the same loop:

ENTER WORLD
 ↓
ATTEMPT TASK
 ↓
WORLD DETERMINES OUTCOME
 ↓
RECORD TRACE
 ↓
MEASURE BEHAVIOUR
 ↓
REPLAY / COMPARE

The two paths into the world differ in one place, before the controls:

Human → controls → simulation → outcome → trace
Agent → intent → validated controls → simulation → outcome → trace

Don't ask the agent whether it succeeded. Ask the world.

An agent can name an intention. It cannot declare that the intention worked. The runtime keeps four things apart, and records each one separately:

agent intention ≠ executed control ≠ environmental outcome ≠ task success

Here is that chain for the coffee delivery in the recorded live Jev run, taken straight from the trace:

An agent cannot mark its own task complete. The environment does. A test plays the whole mission and records the call stack of every coffee pickup, delivery and concert start: each one comes from the game's InteractionManager handling an E press, never from the runtime, a provider or the executor.

The world can also say no. An intention is checked three times: against the schema, against the options that were legal when the agent was asked, and against the world _as it is when the answer arrives_. At sequence 121 of the same run, Jev chose to leave a terminal whose panel had already closed by the time the answer arrived. The trace records it as rejected: "no longer legal in the current world", and nothing executed.

documents.title: satellite-vision-scape — Human and agent, side by side
documents.text:
Human — Agent (Jev, baseline, random, replay)
World — The one running Game instance — The same instance
Perceives — The rendered 3D view, audio, HUD, captions, minimap — A structured observation (svs-agent-observation/v1) of what a player can perceive: HUD, prompts, captions, meters, distances and directions. Text, not pixels or audio
Decides — Every keystroke and mouse movement — One intention at a time, chosen from the legal options on offer right now (≤ 4 requests/s)
Moves by — Keyboard / mouse / touch → InputState — A deterministic executor → SyntheticInput, which has the same interface; the ControlArbiter hands gameplay one or the other
Physics & collisions — Fixed 120 Hz step — Same step, same collision world
Task progress — Advanced by the game's interaction code — Same code, same E press (tested)
Hidden answers — Not shown — Not shown: the frequency only after the Numbers Station says it, terminal targets never
Measured by — svs-agent-evaluation/v1 — The same code
Trace — Control segments, events, metrics, seconds in control — All of that, plus one record per decision
Authority — Can take control at any moment, in the same frame — Can hand control back (request_human); can never seize it or change the world directly

Where they differ, on purpose:

- Perception. The agent reads a description of what a player could perceive, not the pixels. Audio clues reach it as the captions every player also gets. This isolates decision-making from vision; the next-model plan names the measurement that would justify adding screenshots.
- Motor skill. A person steers every frame. An agent chooses _what_ to do ("drive to the technician", "hold the dial up briefly", "wait") and a deterministic executor does _how_: A\* routes, steering, pedals, parking. So an agent run measures judgement, not hand–eye coordination. The executor is identical for every provider, and it drives with a smooth profile while the coffee is aboard, which is part of why agent runs keep most of the coffee.
- Fine controls are the same keys. Tuning a dial is a tap, short hold or long hold of the keys a person uses. There is no intent that names a frequency, a dial value or a coordinate.
- A human has no discrete "decision" to log, so human segments carry events, metrics and control time, but no per-decision records, and cannot be replayed.
- No human reference run is committed yet. People's sessions record the same route samples and world metrics as agents; import an exported run into coffee-run-human-agent to put it beside the baseline (Experiments).

documents.title: satellite-vision-scape — Agents act inside the world. They don't own it.
documents.text:
At any point, the human can reclaim control.

Press H, move, look, press any gameplay key or click outside the agent panel, and control returns in the same frame: the executor stops, every synthetic control is released, the request in flight is aborted and any late answer is discarded as stale. You are where the agent left you, in the same seat, at the same speed, with the same coffee, radio and progress. Nothing resets or teleports. Pausing or leaving the task also hands control back.

Co-pilot turns the agent into an advisor. The panel shows JEV SUGGESTS · Walk to Canteen cart with LET JEV WALK and DISMISS; letting it act delegates exactly one intention, and any input of yours cancels that. The agent never takes control on its own. Suggestions, delegations, cancellations and dismissals are all trace events. …

I make strange things and test whether they work.

Researcher · educator · musician · artist · founder of Vers3Dynamics, an open-source resonant intelligence lab in the Washington, DC area.

A laboratory inside a simulated city. An AI at the wheel of a midnight coffee run. A map where you can redraw a neighborhood and send the same storm through it again. A sensor that has to admit when it cannot know.

I build these things to study a question that keeps changing shape: what gives an intelligent system grounds to believe something—or to act on it? The work brings together experimental worlds, biosignals, statistical measurement, and human authority. My music, paintings, and poetry belong to the same practice: making something difficult to notice available to experience.

Built by one researcher. Held in common. Free to explore.

documents.title: Christopher Woodyard — Enter the work
documents.text:
Start with a question, a place, or a working instrument. These are the projects I would put in your hands first.

01 / R.A.I.N. Lab · A laboratory you can enter:

On the loop: observe → propose → preserve → replay

R.A.I.N. Lab lives inside Lop Nur Twin. A source-linked airfield reconstruction opens into Blacksite, a hidden Bethesda city, and a research room where James, Jasmine, Luca, and Elena bring four perspectives to an investigation.

The distinctive part is the connection between a world, a research proposal, and a retained experiment. A local model can draft a study; host code checks the design and budgets; an operator reviews the plan; the simulator executes it; replay and the registry preserve the outcome. The experimental knowledge graph and research learning engine connect prior records with later investigations. Their presence does not establish general scientific intelligence.

There is another world inside the work: Noeterra, a Rust civilization simulation running as WebAssembly. Rule a nation while other nations act under their own rule-based policies, or use the same engine as a substrate for reviewed civilization experiments. Public play uses no model; model rulers and live research require the local workbench.

Explore the twin → · Play Noeterra → · Inspect the evidence → · Run the lab locally →

Actual project captures: a scripted offline meeting and a simulated experiment record. Replay establishes computational consistency, not a discovery about people or physical equipment.

A recorded live Gemma experiment passed replay and entered the registry, but failed its numerical accuracy guards. Its scientific verdict stayed inconclusive. That boundary is part of the instrument.

Evidence ladder: EXECUTABLE · OBSERVED (scripted and live-model-designed simulator experiments; no physical or general scientific validation).

The original james_library runtime is archived. Its migration record documents the port into the current lab; its older experimental results remain historical evidence.

Historical evidence ladder: EXECUTABLE · OBSERVED (seeded quotation checks and simulated controls; same-seed reruns).

02 / Pine Gap · Put an agent somewhere it can fail:

On the loop: act → measure → preserve → replay, inside a simulation

Pine Gap is a playable browser world: deliver coffee, drive past radomes, follow a numbers station, find a concert. My own music plays on the radio.

Underneath is an instrument for comparing behavior. Human controls, scripted policies, and model decisions reach the same movement and task mechanics. The simulator determines the consequences. Traces retain decisions, handovers, collisions, refusals, and outcomes.

That makes an interesting question observable: did the agent solve the task, or did the environment make it easy? Recorded live Jev sessions exist alongside scripted baselines. They are case studies, not a repeated-trial success rate.

Play → · Watch the scripted baseline → · Inspect a live run →

Public play and the scripted baseline need no key. Live Jev requires local setup and a TypeSafe key. See the gameplay still.

Evidence ladder: EXECUTABLE · OBSERVED (recorded live-agent case studies and paired scripted experiments; simulated world).

03 / Quantum Noise Profiler · Can a warning earn your trust?

On the loop: observe → measure → preserve

Quantum Noise Profiler studies qubit-noise monitoring: how to notice meaningful deterioration without confusing a changed workload with changed hardware, and when to withhold an estimate.

It distinguishes vendor observations, workload-inferred values, and dedicated probe measurements. Its monitoring methods track a session error budget; its fits and forecasts can refuse unsupported answers. …

documents.text:
These projects develop other parts of the practice. Each has its own scope; shared ideas do not mean every repository is wired into one running system.

- Anna / R.A.I.N. DataMatrix Engine — self-hosted research search with hybrid retrieval, inspectable source passages, citation exports, and research records that can be checked for source drift. Built on Anna's Archive's search architecture. A valid citation does not establish factual support.
- IONS-X Deep Emergence Lab — collective sensing in a changing synthetic field. Paired coupled and uncoupled runs ask which associations survive removal of the injected structure; they do not demonstrate consciousness or causality.

- Sentinel — an account-free sound and breathing studio with adjustable tones, noise, pacing, and local session records. It generates an experience; it does not measure physiology or establish therapeutic effects.

documents.title: Christopher Woodyard — The idea
documents.text:
An answer is the beginning of an investigation. I want to see what was observed, which explanation was proposed, what the system was allowed to do, and what actually happened.

One loop runs through the lab:

observe → propose → validate → authorize → act → measure → preserve → replay

The authorize step belongs to a person, or to a deterministic policy a person wrote. A model's inference is not evidence, its confidence is not permission, and a beautiful simulation is not a measurement of the real world.

Intelligence may propose. Evidence must be checked. Authority stays with the human.

documents.title: Christopher Woodyard — What the evidence says
documents.text:
The point is to build things that can tell me when I am wrong. Failed tests stay in the record, including when later work improves the method.

Open seven findings, failures, and their source records:

- R.A.I.N.: The live Gemma oscillator experiment replayed successfully but failed both analytical accuracy guards. Its conclusion stayed inconclusive. Record. Historically, the quotation gate also rejected genuine quotes after typography normalization. Archived failure.
- Quantum Noise Profiler: The follow-up repaired two earlier failure modes in simulation; CUSUM matched its operational performance, and hardware validation remains undone. Results.
- Mannahatta: Routed accumulation did not locate held-out flood reports better than low elevation. The map's usefulness as a question does not validate it as a forecast. Holdout.
- TRIAD: On 5,078 outcome-grounded claims, its decision cost was 0.159, versus 0.121 for the blind statistical reviewer and 0.125 for endorsing nothing. The same-model-family AI comparators and lack of human adjudication limit the test. Milestone 8.
- DRR: Its preregistered NOAA QBO structural-change comparison exceeded the permitted false-alarm rate. External evidence.
- James: Earlier small-model sessions confused simulator findings with real-world evidence or claimed authority the model did not have. Later implementation checks do not erase those failures. Historical session.
- Pine Gap: Paired scripted runs exposed a control-size failure: graded dial turns locked terminals; long holds did not. A later live Free Roam run completed its task but recorded a pedestrian collision. Scripted experiment · Live trace.

The public ledger separates implementation, recorded observation, independent reproduction, and external support. …

documents.title: TRIAD (topherchris420/triad)
documents.text:
When should a sensor refuse to answer?

*An open Rust research instrument for selective prediction, evidence sufficiency,
and the limits of confident inference.*

A system can converge on an answer and still be wrong. It can report uncertainty
and still underestimate its errors. It can carry an evidence record and still make
a claim that the record does not support.

TRIAD makes those gaps inspectable. Built at Vers3Dynamics, it evaluates errors among accepted predictions, tests explicit
rules for assessing reliability claims, and traces its findings back to frozen
protocols and machine-readable results. The work began with a simulated capacitive
sensor and expanded into experiments on real prediction data.

Research status: TRIAD's added warning and evidence rules have not established
an advantage over strong existing practice. Its sensor studies failed numerical
readiness gates. The repository provides runnable measurement tools and archived
negative findings; predictive superiority and hardware confidence remain unvalidated.
Its newest result is statistical engineering, not a sensor finding: in a pre-registered
simulation, established risk-control tests certified the same refusal guarantee with
a tenth of the labeled data (Milestone 9).

documents.title: TRIAD — What you can use
documents.text:
Your question — TRIAD provides — Start here
How often are the answers I accept wrong? — Classification and regression evaluation, risk–coverage curves, calibration diagnostics, and sequence/cluster bootstrap intervals — Selective-risk quickstart
Does this evidence support this particular claim? — Typed claims, explicit scope checks, evidence provenance, and four inspectable decision outcomes — Evidence-sufficiency method
Do extra warnings improve decisions on real streams? — Frozen Electricity and Bike Sharing benchmarks, simpler comparators, and independent verification code — Real-data reproduction
Can a fixed abstention policy meet declared risk and coverage bounds? — A conservative controller calibrated on independent labeled sequences; it refuses certification when evidence is insufficient — Portable components
How many labeled sessions must I collect before a refusal policy can be certified? — A certifier that provably dominates that controller, a variance-adaptive betting variant, and a sample-size planner — Certification method
Are my sensor recordings structurally usable? — Ten-channel capture validation, unit checks, covariance and reference-drift diagnostics — Capture contract
Why can a position estimator appear certain and still fail? — A 2D electrostatic model, inverse estimator, ambiguity diagnostics, and numerical error audits — Physical model

The generic evaluator works with saved predictions and labels; it does not require
the FEM sensor simulation. Selective risk is an established metric, credited to
the selective-classification literature. TRIAD supplies one implementation and
tests additional ideas around it.

documents.title: TRIAD — Start with the evidence
documents.text:
Use a Rust toolchain with Cargo and a compatible native linker. The locked test
suite runs in Linux and Windows CI. Python is needed for claim checking and the
independent study verifiers; each real-data study lists its own dependencies.

git clone https://github.com/topherchris420/triad.git
cd triad
git switch master
cargo run --release --locked -- metrology evaluate --input examples/predictions.json --output my-report.json
cargo run --release --locked -- metrology validate --input my-report.json

This small fixture produces my-report.json and my-report.md without running
FEM. The JSON separates calibration-fixed evaluation from retrospective
matched-coverage analysis. Read report.overall.operational for realized coverage,
selective error risk, accepted count, and accepted-error count. A null risk means
no accepted predictions, not zero errors. Use a new output path for each run;
the metrology commands refuse to overwrite reports.

To evaluate your own model, follow the
triad-metrology-1 example. Supply disjoint calibration
and test records with predictions, truth, uncertainty scores, and sequence IDs.
Smaller scores mean more confident. Fix the threshold using calibration scores,
then measure the realized coverage and risk on the test split. Target coverage is
not a guarantee of future coverage or error control.

The quickstart also includes a
standard-library Python reference, checked against Rust in CI, for calculating
the metric without building TRIAD.

Explore the other interfaces and check the archived claims:

The abstention and capture examples are synthetic fixtures. Both abstention
commands intentionally refuse certification because the calibration sample is
insufficient. The planner shows how many independent sessions would be needed. The capture inspector checks recordings; it does not infer physical
positions or validate hardware performance.

documents.title: TRIAD — The measurement at the center
documents.text:
Coverage asks how often the system answers. Selective risk asks **how often
those accepted answers are wrong**. Report them together.

Let the acceptance rule be $g_\tau(x)=\mathbf{1}\{s(x)\leq\tau\}$ and let
$\ell(f(x),y)$ be a declared loss bounded in $[0,1]$:

$$
C(\tau)=\mathbb{E}[g_\tau(X)],\qquad
R(\tau)=\frac{\mathbb{E}[\ell(f(X),Y)\,g_\tau(X)]}{C(\tau)}.
$$

Risk is undefined when coverage is zero. TRIAD uses an error-event loss:
misclassification for classification, or exceeding a declared error tolerance for
regression. Threshold ties are accepted. A lower risk obtained by answering fewer
questions requires a coverage comparison or an explicit cost for abstaining.

Two evaluations serve different purposes. A calibration-fixed threshold can
be applied to future inputs, but its test coverage can differ from the target.
Retrospective ranking compares methods at matched test coverage, but does not
supply a deployable threshold. See the method definition
for score conventions, tie handling, AURC, and bootstrap assumptions.

documents.title: TRIAD — The research arc, machine-checked
documents.text:
The question widened from Can this position be trusted? to *Does this evidence
support the claim being made?* The table below keeps the answers attached to their
archived sources, including failed gates and negative comparisons.

Milestone — Question — What the archived evidence says — Status — Source
:--: — --- — --- — --- — ---
2 — Does an optimizer's convergence flag tell you the answer is trustworthy? — No. 451 nonconvergence flags among 1,080 positions, yet only 10 of the 20 errors above 5 mm were flagged — Descriptive, synthetic pilot — evaluation.json
3 — Does a physics-informed rejection score (D) beat posterior expected-error rejection (C2)? — No. At matched 80% acceptance D accepted 37 errors above 5 mm versus 42 for C2, a risk reduction of 0.174 percentage points against a 2-point threshold. Worst surrogate discrepancy 37.78 noise units — Hypothesis not supported; numerical gate failed — summary.json
4 — Is the simulated sensor accurate to within its own noise? — No. Local interpolation cut interpolation discrepancy from 29.86 to 2.28 noise units, but mesh discrepancy stays at 9.82 and total mismatch at 10.48 — Numerical readiness false — numerical-components-v4.json
6 — Do validity warnings add value on real data (OpenML Electricity)? — No. Accuracy 65.57% (logistic) and 66.00% (forest). Gating cut logistic coverage to 55.55% while accepted error risk moved only from 31.19% to 30.39% — Negative — report.json
7 — Do evidence-qualified trust decisions beat standard monitoring (UCI Bike Sharing)? — No. TRIAD minus standard monitoring: Δ cost +0.0049 (ridge) and +0.0062 (gradient boosting) per hour — Negative; replicates Milestone 6 — report.json
7 — Do explicit claim-relative rules catch unsupported claims that standard checks miss? — 43/47 versus 20/47 with 0 false rejections, on an author-constructed suite — Engineering capability only — report.json
8 — Do those rules beat reviewers written without seeing TRIAD, judged by real outcomes? — No. Decision cost 0.159 versus 0.121 (blind statistical reviewer, Δ +0.038, inferior) and 0.160 (blind checklist). Never endorsing costs 0.125. 5,078 claims, five datasets — Not established (pre-registered) — report.json
8 — Does the Milestone 7 advantage over standard checks survive world truth? — Yes. Δ −0.172 versus standard checks and −0.050 versus checks with scope, but blind reviewers reproduce it — Replicated, not distinctive — report.json
8 — Where do the rules fail? — Next-week operational claims: 7 of 19 false ones endorsed, because the rules do not forecast — Repair needs a new frozen test — report.json
9 — Can established risk-control tests certify the same refusal guarantee with fewer independent sessions? — Yes. 80% certification at 2,500 sessions (Hoeffding–Bentkus) and 1,000 (betting) versus 25,000 (legacy). 0 dominance violations; no false certification above δ — Supported; pre-registered simulation, not real data — report.json
9 — Does treating dependent frames as independent cause false certification? — Not shown. …

documents.title: DC4 News - Washington DC Local News — COVCOM Architecture (Covert Communication)
documents.text:
The hidden command flow now uses a small COVCOM layer (src/lib/covcom.ts) to centralize, type, and make it easy to extend covert triggers.

- Signal normalization: incoming input is normalized before matching.
- Channel registry: each covert channel defines aliases + a resolver.
- Action protocol: channels return typed actions (redirect, open-contact, or none) consumed by UI.
- UI decoupling: DCNewsLanding calls resolveCovcomSignal(...) instead of embedding ad-hoc checks.

Current channels:
- library-access via 137 or library
- contact-channel via contact or signal
